concepts.quote: No, A has two conditions and B has only one.
concepts.why: The answer is wrong: B also tests x > 0 in its ?: expression, and both A and B leave y unchanged when x < 0, set it to 0 when x == 0 and set it to 1 when x > 0. Counting the conditions on the surface is not a correct Java reading of the if statements.
The answer says nothing about arrays or aliasing.
The answer uses the number of conditions in A's else-if chain to claim a different result, but the else-if chain sets y exactly as B's nested if with ?: does.
The answer says nothing about identifiers.
